A '''model''' of [[Mon Calamari]] [[cruiser]]<ref name="Tweet 1" /> was used by the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Navy]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]], a pan-[[The galaxy|galactic]] conflict between the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[Galactic Empire]]. The [[warship]] was capable of traveling in [[Realspace|space]] via [[engine]]s. It had bulbous yet slim features, with a thin protrusion at the rear.<ref name="Episode VI" />

Shortly prior to the [[Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Episode VI" /> in [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> the Alliance gathered its [[Alliance Military|forces]] in the [[Sullust system]] in a [[staging area]] to launch its attack on the Empire's [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]], located in the [[Moddell sector]] in [[orbit]] of the [[Endor|Forest Moon of Endor]]. At least one Mon Calamari cruiser of this type was present in addition to a wide variety of warships shortly prior to the [[fleet]] jumping into [[hyperspace]] to commence the battle.<ref name="Episode VI" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:ROTJ-Rebel-Fleet-Storyboard.png|thumb|left|240px|The ''Return of the Jedi'' storyboard featuring the Mon Calamari cruiser, according to Paul Duncan.]]
The Mon Calamari cruiser debuted in the [[1983]] [[original trilogy]] film, {{Film|VI}}, appearing in the assortment of rebel starships prior to the Battle of Endor and located in the background.<ref name="Episode VI" /> According to ''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes IV–VI, 1977–1983]]'' author [[Paul Duncan]], concept art of the cruiser was created for the film, and the cruiser's model was featured in storyboards during the film's production. Duncan additionally stated that there are images of the model ship in the [[Lucasfilm Archives]], but he did not have space to include any in ''The Star Wars Archives'',<ref name="Tweet 1" /> which was published in [[2018]].<ref name="SWArchives">''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes IV–VI, 1977–1983]]''</ref>

The storyboard depicting the Rebel Fleet, along with the cruiser, had appeared in ''[[Star Wars Storyboards: The Original Trilogy]]'', which was edited by [[Jonathan W. Rinzler]] and published in [[2014]].<ref name="Storyboards">''[[Star Wars Storyboards: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref> Duncan confirmed that he saw the images but does not possess copies of them, and he stated that the pictures he saw were in the model shop, so they were neither complete nor detailed shots of the cruiser's film model.<ref name="Tweet 2">{{Twitter|kershed|status/1665431296636514304|[[Paul Duncan]]|date=2023-06-04|quote=I saw the images, but do not have copies of them. The pix were in the model shop, so not complete/detailed shots.|archivedate=20230604190830}}</ref>
